# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).
data.title: Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

# F6 — Lazy per-command imports via a command registry

Implements desired change #2: replace the 35 eager `import XCommand` lines with a name → `() => import('./commands/x.js')` registry, resolved on demand. Only the command that actually runs loads its module; `--help` and bare `wl` may load all (rare).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/cli-main.ts` registers commands through the registry; no static imports of `./commands/*` remain.
- A single-command invocation loads only that command module (verified by F5's isolation test); `--help` and bare `wl` load all command modules and produce identical grouped help output.
- Plugin loading and `initializeRuntime` ordering is unchanged for commands that need them; commands that do not touch the DB still avoid opening it (visible in F1 spawn record kinds).
- Graceful degradation (parent AC5): a registry resolution error logs one warning, falls back to eager full registration, then dispatches the command; covered by F5's fault-injection test.
- Full suite green; existing read-cache, e2e and spawn-reduction suites unchanged (parent AC4).

## Minimal Implementation

1. Declare a registry mapping each name in the existing `builtInCommandNames` set to a dynamic import of its module.
2. Resolve the single command token from argv before `program.parse()` and register only that command (falling back to all for `--help`/bare invocation/unknown token).
3. Keep help grouping metadata independent of module loading.

**Key Files:**
- `src/cli-main.ts`
- `src/command-registry.ts`
- `src/commands/*.ts`
- `src/plugin-loader.ts`

## Dependencies

- F5 (tests first).

# F7 — Fast-path import slimming to the 0.5 s / 60 MB budget

Parent AC1 sets a deliberately tight budget: p95 <= 0.5 s wall and <= 60 MB peak RSS for warm cache hits, against a bare-node floor of 0.35 s / 58 MB and today's `read-cache-cli` graph at 0.46 s / 61 MB. After F4/F6 the fast path still imports the read-cache graph, so this item shaves it until the budget is met and then freezes the win.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Warm cache-hit `wl next --json`, `wl list --status open --json` and `wl --version` on the reference host: p95 wall <= 0.5 s and peak RSS <= 60 MB (F2 benchmark, >= 10 runs), with before and after numbers quoted in a comment.
- The fast-path graph no longer imports `commander`, `better-sqlite3`, `plugin-loader`, `cli-utils`, `lib/runtime`, `config` or schema/validation plumbing; the F2 ratchet is tightened and its budget updated to the parent AC1 target (p95 <= 0.5 s, peak RSS <= 60 MB).
- The specific reductions are recorded (for example: version read from `src/version.ts`, minimal worklog-dir resolution on the fast path, hashing/crypto deferred to the miss path, argv handling without `cli-utils`).
- No correctness change: cache keys, freshness and JSON bytes identical (parent AC4); full suite green.
- If the 60 MB target proves unreachable, the item records the measured floor with evidence and raises an OPEN QUESTION on the parent instead of silently relaxing the AC.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Re-run the F2 harness and profile the fast-path import graph.
2. Replace heavy imports still reachable from `read-cache-cli` (worklog-dir resolution, hashing, argv helpers) with minimal equivalents, deferring them to miss paths.
3. Tighten the F2 allowlist to the final set so the win cannot silently regress.

**Key Files:**
- `src/cli.ts`
- `src/read-cache-cli.ts`
- `src/read-cache.ts`
- `src/worklog-paths.ts`
- `tests/cli/startup-import-budget.test.ts`
- `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts`

## Dependencies

- F2 (harness and baseline)
- F4 (entry split)
- F6 (lazy registry, for the non-cache-hit command cost)
data.title: Fast-path import slimming to the 0.5 s / 60 MB budget

# F10 — Verify the >= 60 % CPU-second reduction per refresh cycle

Parent AC2's measurement and decision point. With F1 instrumentation, measure total CPU-seconds per 30 s refresh cycle across >= 4 panes on one shared worklog dir, before and after the fast path, and only then decide whether herdr read coalescing is additionally required.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A repeatable measurement procedure is recorded (env `WL_SPAWN_COUNT_FILE`, 4 panes running the herdr query set over one 30 s cycle, warm cache) with the exact command quoted in a comment.
- Baseline and after numbers are both quoted in comments on this item and on the parent: total CPU-seconds, spawn count, cache-hit count, p95 per-spawn wall time and RSS.
- After <= 0.4x baseline total CPU-seconds (>= 60 % reduction) is demonstrated, or the shortfall is quantified with the dominant remaining cost identified.
- If the target is missed, the item records which lever is needed. Given herdr already has in-flight memoisation and in-process SQLite reads (`WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG`, `WL-0MV6C6SLB005HX7B`), it either (a) implements a bounded, stateless coalescing refinement in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` (one consolidated read per refresh tick) or (b) files a `discovered-from` child when the change exceeds this item's scope.
- No correctness regression: herdr refresh output is unchanged for the same DB state and the spawn-reduction simulation test still passes.
- Covers parent AC2: total CPU-seconds per 30 s refresh cycle across >= 4 panes on a shared worklog dir drops >= 60 % versus current behaviour, measured by the env-gated spawn instrumentation with per-process CPU time; baseline and after numbers quoted.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Build a 4-pane measurement harness reusing the patterns in `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts` plus F1 aggregation.
2. Measure the pre-split build first (worktree of `dev`, or `WL_CACHE_DISABLED=1` for the read-work baseline), then re-measure after F4 to F7.
3. Record numbers and the lever decision in comments.

**Key Files:**
- `src/spawn-counter.ts`
- `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts`
- `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts`

## Dependencies

- F1 (CPU and RSS instrumentation)
- F6 (lazy per-command imports)
- F7 (fast-path budget)
data.title: Verify >=60% CPU-second reduction per refresh cycle

## Goal

Make the Worklog extension footer show the model that is **actually** serving the session immediately after a mid-session model switch — invalidating the stale resolved value and falling back to the selected model's own `provider/id` when no proxy header can ever arrive.

## Context

Parent: `WL-0MVGEB3IP002V8IB`. Today `model_select` updates only `_selectedModel`, so the footer pairs the new alias with the previous resolved model; for non-proxy providers (`deepseek`, `opencode`, `opencode-go` in `~/.pi/agent/models.json`) the `x-resolved-model` header never arrives and the stale value persists for the rest of the session.

## Implementation (surgical — no speculative refactor)

1. **Invalidate on selection** — in the `model_select` handler of `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/model-display.ts`, clear `_resolvedModel` to `null` for every source (`set` / `cycle` / `restore`) and notify `_onModelChange` exactly once so the footer re-renders to `<newAlias> → (resolving)`.
2. **Non-proxy fallback** — when the selected model's `provider` is not the Local Proxy, set `_resolvedModel` to `${model.provider}/${model.id}` (the *selected* model's provider/id — never `modelOverrides`) instead of leaving it `null`.
3. **Proxy-provider selections** — when the provider **is** the Local Proxy, leave `_resolvedModel` as `null` so the honest `(resolving)` state shows until a real `x-resolved-model` header arrives.
4. **Shared provider-name constant** — reuse the canonical `Local Proxy` name. The constant currently exists as a **private** `LOCAL_PROVIDER_NAME` in `packages/shared/src/lease-release.ts` and is **not exported**. Recommended: add the `export` keyword there (a one-line, non-behavioural change; `packages/shared` is not the local proxy and the extension already imports `@worklog/shared/lease-release`). If the producer prefers to honour the "changes confined to `packages/tui/extensions`" constraint literally, define a local constant in `model-display.ts` that cites the shared convention in a comment. Record whichever option is taken in a comment on this item.
5. **Fail-open** — a missing/unknown provider, missing model, or unreadable config must not throw; degrade to `null` (→ `(resolving)`) exactly as today. No new I/O on the render path.
6. **No render changes expected** — `session-health.ts` already handles a `null` resolved value; touch it only if the new tests prove otherwise, and then preserve right-alignment and the width budget.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `model_select` with `source: "set"`, `"cycle"` or `"restore"` leaves `getResolvedModel() === null` and `getSelectedModel()` set to the new id, and fires `onModelChange` once.
2. Selecting a model whose provider is not the Local Proxy sets `getResolvedModel()` to that model's own `${provider}/${id}` in the same handler run (no `(resolving)` phase for non-proxy providers).
3. Selecting a Local Proxy model keeps `getResolvedModel() === null` until an `x-resolved-model` header arrives; subsequent proxy responses behave exactly as before (lowercase/uppercase header extraction, no-op on identical values, `onModelChange` firing).
4. A missing model, missing provider, or unavailable/unknown config does not throw and degrades to `null` (fail-open).
5. The provider-name check reuses the canonical `Local Proxy` constant (exported from `@worklog/shared/lease-release`, or a documented local equivalent) — no duplicated magic strings without a comment.
6. All tests added by the sibling test item pass, and no pre-existing test in `model-display.test.ts` or `session-health.test.ts` regresses.
7. `session-health.ts` is unchanged unless a test proves a render change is required; any such change preserves right-alignment, truncation and width handling.

## Key Files

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/model-display.ts` — the only expected production change (handler + fallback helper).
- `packages/shared/src/lease-release.ts` — optional one-line `export` of `LOCAL_PROVIDER_NAME` (decision recorded in a comment).
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.ts` — verify only; do not change speculatively.

## Notes

- Depends on the test item — do not start until those tests exist and are red.
- Prerequisite test item: "Tests: mid-session model-switch invalidation and non-proxy fallback".
- Keep the single-slot `onModelChange` and the `session_start` `!_selectedModel` guard untouched (latent, out of scope — see parent Risks).
- Run tests only via the test skill (`/skill:test`, changed scope).
data.title: Implement: invalidate resolved model on model_select with non-proxy fallback

## Goal

Document the new mid-session model-display semantics and prove the whole change is green, so an operator or auditor reading the footer can trust what it claims.

## Context

Parent: `WL-0MVGEB3IP002V8IB`. Two behaviour changes land in the sibling implementation item: `model_select` now invalidates the resolved model, and a non-proxy selected model falls back to its own `provider/id`. The README currently documents only the four pre-existing Line-3 states and describes `model_select` merely as "Refresh footer display".

## Scope

### 1. Documentation

`packages/tui/extensions/README.md`:

- **"Model/Provider Display (Line 3)" state table** — add rows for:
  - model switched mid-session, proxy response not yet received → `plan → (resolving)`;
  - non-proxy provider selected → `plan → deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`;
  - and note that a mid-session `model_select` discards the previously resolved value.
- **"Event Tracking" table** — change the `model_select` row meaning from "Refresh footer display" to reflect that it also invalidates the cached resolved model and derives the `provider/id` fallback for non-proxy providers.
- **Model ID row in the status-entries table** (line ~94) — keep it consistent with the new states.
- Code comments in `model-display.ts` — the module header currently says `model_select` "does not display the model alias"; update it to describe invalidation and the non-proxy fallback.
- Check for any docs-site / wiki page that mirrors the Line-3 state table and update it to match (search `docs/` and the repo for `(resolving)`); if a mirrored page exists and is out of this repo, record where it lives in a comment instead of editing it.

### 2. Verification

- Run the full project test suite through the test skill (`/skill:test`, full scope) and confirm it is green.
- Walk the parent's AC1–AC7 and record a one-line met/not-met note per AC in a comment on this item (AC coverage evidence for the parent's audit).
- Confirm the `(resolving)`, right-alignment and width-handling behaviours (`WL-0MRO7LWIX001516P`, `WL-0MSMDYJ3X00895MP`, `WL-0MSHENVKR002HZT5`) are covered by passing tests — cite the test names.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` Line-3 state table includes the mid-session invalidation state (`<alias> → (resolving)`) and the non-proxy fallback state (`<alias> → <provider>/<id>`).
2. The README "Event Tracking" row for `model_select` describes invalidation of the resolved model plus the non-proxy `provider/id` fallback.
3. `model-display.ts` module/function comments describe the new `model_select` semantics (no stale "does not display the model alias" wording left contradicting behaviour).
4. Any other repo page mirroring the Line-3 state table (found via a `(resolving)` search) is updated, or its out-of-repo location recorded in a comment.
5. The full project test suite passes via the test skill; the run is recorded in a comment on this item.
6. A comment records AC1–AC7 of the parent with met/not-met evidence, including the names of the tests that guard `(resolving)`, right-alignment and width handling.

## Key Files

- `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — Line-3 state table, Event Tracking table, status-entries Model ID row.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/model-display.ts` — documentation comments only (no behavioural edits in this item).
- (search) `docs/` and repo-wide `(resolving)` references for mirrored tables.

## Notes

- Depends on the implementation item; the suite must not be run as the "green gate" before the implementation lands.
- Documentation-only edits here must not contradict the implemented behaviour — re-read `model-display.ts` after implementation and document what it actually does.

## F6 implementation summary

**New `src/command-registry.ts`** — the 30 eager `import XCommand` lines in `src/cli-main.ts` are gone:
- `COMMAND_LOADERS`: name → `() => import('./commands/x.js')` (32 names; `audit-show`/`audit-set` share the audit-result module loader and `audit-waive`/`audit-unwaive` the audit-waive loader, so each module's `register()` runs once — no duplicate commands).
- `registerBuiltInCommands(ctx, argv, {loaders, onLoad, warn})`: a single-command invocation loads only that command; bare `wl`, `--help`/`-h`, unknown commands and `completion` (whose output enumerates every command) register the full set.
- Graceful degradation (parent AC5): a rejecting loader logs exactly one warning and falls back to eager full registration, attempting every other module so one broken module cannot take the CLI down.
- `BUILT_IN_COMMAND_NAMES` (ordered) now feeds the help-grouping set in `cli-main.ts`; `applyWorklogDirOverrideFromArgv`/`--worklog-dir` handling and `loadPlugins` ordering are unchanged.

**F5 specs finalised**: the two RED-pinned `it.fails` specs flipped to real assertions (`src/command-registry.ts` now exists), with the observer semantics documented (`onLoad` fires per attempted load) and `BUILT_IN_COMMAND_NAMES.length` used for the fallback bound.

**Parity evidence**: `dist/cli.js --help` is **byte-identical** to the pre-F6 build (registration order preserved, including the `cleanup-worktree`/`completion` ordering); `wl completion bash` again lists all 32 built-ins; `wl audit-show --help`, `wl cleanup-worktree --help`, unknown-command error/exit and the cache-hit spawn records are unchanged.

Full canonical suite green (tests/cli 104 files; tests/unit 43 files).
